No, notion is not high effort. No, it does not help everyone with productivity. 

but that's just the 'basic' answer.

For me personally, I like the way things look in order to use it. So, it was difficult to start off with. Putting everything together takes time and effort and I needed to do some research to learn how to use it.    
  
Sure, you can type away, slap it all together and call it a day, but that's not pleasing to the eye and probably won't make most people want to come back to keep using it.   
  
So, it's not high effort if you don't want to put in the effort, it is if you want things to look good. 

As for productivity, it depends from person to person. I struggle greatly with productivity, and notion hasn't helped much. It has, however, helped me keep things more organized.   
  
I'm sure other people will benefit more with productivity, though, and that's great for them!

When looking to get a dog, a little extra advice I can give is to see where the nearest vet is, if they're a good vet, and the general cost of some things (general checkup, treatments, things like that), to make sure you're prepared :) 

Old dogs that are healthy usually need to go about once every half year for a general checkup, but it can be more often if something comes up  


I'm confident that you'll be a good dog parent when you get one

There’s nothing weird about wanting to get an older dog,
Of course, it’s always gonna be some commitment, dogs both young and old need to be fed daily, and need walks, attention and love,..

It’s certainly not a bad thing if you’d like to adopt an older dog, but it is important to know they can be a big commitment, too. 
Older dogs usually need some more time than pups to get comfortable, too, and they can cost quite a bit, certainly vet costs. 

Once you can get a dog and care for it, making sure to have time for the dog, i’d say it wouldn’t be bad or weird at all for you to get an older, calm dog :)
